Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Somalia's 2023 Data Protection Act provides for the right to an effective remedy and the DPA has an Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedure for handling complaints. The 2012 Constitution guarantees the right to privacy (Article 13). Individuals can object to data processing and seek redress through the DPA. There is no evidence of a specialized ID-specific court mechanism or judicial oversight body dedicated to digital ID. General constitutional protections and DPA complaint mechanisms apply.
revision_notes: Fetched both cited sources. TechHive Advisory confirms the 2023 Data Protection Act (Law No. 005) provides data subjects a right to an effective remedy and that the DPA operates an Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedure for complaints; Wikipedia confirms the Act's structure and 2012 constitutional privacy basis. No evidence found of an ID-specific judicial review mechanism; oversight is general (constitutional/DPA), not ID-specific. Score of 2 confirmed.
revised_comments: Judicial oversight of Somalia's digital ID system operates through general mechanisms rather than an ID-specific court process. The 2012 Provisional Constitution guarantees the right to privacy (Article 13), and the 2023 Data Protection Act (Law No. 005) gives data subjects the right to an effective remedy, backed by the Data Protection Authority's Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedure for complaints. There is no dedicated judicial mechanism specific to the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA) or the digital ID system.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: The 2023 Data Protection Act includes provisions on limitations on data sharing between the ID system and other government entities/third parties, cross-border transfer restrictions, and requirements for data controllers. The NIRA Act Law 009/2023 also references limitations on information sharing. However, the DPA Guidance and rules are still being operationalized and experts note the data sharing framework is partial—rules exist but full implementation and enforcement is ongoing.
revision_notes: TechHive Advisory (fetched) confirms the 2023 Data Protection Act sets out lawful bases for processing, cross-border transfer restrictions, and controller/processor obligations, with the DPA issuing an Implementation Regulation and Guidance from 2024. The NIRA Act PDF (upload.wikimedia.org) returned a 403 error and could not be fetched to verify the ID-specific data-sharing provisions cited in the original comments. The mof.gov.so TOR is a 2019 pre-legislative design document, not evidence of the current rules status. Only the general Data Protection Act provisions could be independently verified; the NIRA Act's specific information-sharing clauses could not be checked on this pass. The 'partially available' score is plausible and broadly consistent with available evidence but not fully verified against the primary ID law text.
revised_comments: Somalia's data-sharing rules for identity-related personal data are partially established. The 2023 Data Protection Act sets out lawful bases for processing, obligations on data controllers and processors, and restrictions on cross-border transfers, with the Data Protection Authority (inaugurated February 2024) having published implementation guidance and an Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedure. The National Identification and Registration Act (Law No. 009 of 2023) also contains provisions on information sharing by NIRA. Full public documentation and enforcement of ID-specific data-sharing agreements remains at an early stage.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Somalia enacted the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023) on March 23, 2023—the country's first comprehensive data protection law. Grounded in Article 13 of the 2012 Constitution (right to privacy), it covers rights of data subjects, obligations of controllers/processors, lawful bases for processing, breach notification, cross-border transfer restrictions, and DPIAs. The Somalia Data Protection Authority (DPA) was formally inaugurated in February 2024.
revision_notes: All three cited sources fetched and confirmed. Somalia enacted the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023) on 23 March 2023, its first comprehensive data protection law, grounded in Article 13 of the 2012 Constitution. The Somalia Data Protection Authority was inaugurated on 24 February 2024 (confirmed by africadataprotection.org and lawgratis.com) and has since issued Implementation Regulation and Guidance (confirmed by TechHive Advisory). Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed.
revised_comments: Somalia has enacted comprehensive national data protection legislation covering personal data linked to the ID system. The Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023), effective from 23 March 2023, establishes data subject rights, controller and processor obligations, lawful bases for processing, cross-border transfer restrictions and breach notification requirements. The Somalia Data Protection Authority was inaugurated on 24 February 2024 and has since issued implementation guidance and an Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedure.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The NIRA Act (Law 009/2023) and associated regulations establish the national ID as legal proof of identity for use across public and private services. NIRA issues a credential that serves as an official, verifiable identity document. The Somalia government has mandated the ID as a legal requirement for passport applications (from September 2025) and domestic travel (from January 2026), confirming its status as legal proof of identity.
revision_notes: allAfrica (fetched, 8 August 2025) confirms Somalia will require the national ID to obtain passports from 1 September 2025 and for domestic travel from 1 January 2026, establishing the credential's function as legal proof of identity in practice. NIRA's own site (fetched) describes the ID document as serving as 'official proof of identity ... used for various government and administrative purposes.' The NIRA Act PDF itself returned a 403 error and could not be independently fetched to cite the specific statutory provision, but the corroborating operational evidence is sufficient to confirm legal-proof status. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed and evidence updated to reflect the more recent 2025 mandate.
revised_comments: Somalia's National Identification Number and card, issued under the National Identification and Registration Act (Law No. 009 of 2023), function as legal proof of identity. From 1 September 2025 the national ID became a prerequisite for passport applications, and from 1 January 2026 it is required for domestic travel, formalising its role as the primary identity credential for government and administrative purposes.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Somalia enacted the National Identification and Registration Act (Law No. 009, March 2023), establishing NIRA as the legal authority for national ID. This was accompanied by the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005, March 2023). Both laws were approved by both chambers of parliament and signed by the President. A legal framework specifically governing digital ID and data protection is clearly in place.

The NIRA Act PDF itself returned a 403 error and could not be independently fetched. Note: subsequent commentary (WardheerNews, SomalilandCurrent, November 2025) raises constitutional questions about whether the Act received adequate Upper House/Federal Member State consultation, but does not dispute that the legislation was enacted and remains in force. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed.
revised_comments: Formal legislation governs digital identity in Somalia. The National Identification and Registration Act (Law No. 009 of March 2023) establishes the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA) and its legal mandate, and is complemented by the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023) governing personal data. Both were approved by parliament and signed into law by the President.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The National Identification and Registration Act (Law 009/2023) does not explicitly set a minimum age threshold but the system appears targeted at adults. The NIRA website and government directives reference the ID as required for passports, banking, domestic travel, and school/university enrollment, suggesting the primary eligible population is 18+. Parents register teenagers urgently for school and university admissions. No evidence of enrollment below age 10 or at birth. The minimum age of enrollment is effectively 17+.
revision_notes: NIRA's registration page (fetched) describes the biographic data captured (name, parents' names, date/place of birth, etc.) but does not state a minimum enrollment age. Somali Magazine (fetched) covers the biometric ID rollout generally without citing any age threshold. The mof.gov.so Digital ID Legal Framework TOR (fetched, a 2019 pre-legislative design document) states the ID system 'will strive to provide a unique identity from birth to death, with close linkages to civil registration' - in tension with the original inference of '>17' drawn from adult-oriented use cases (passports, banking, travel). The NIRA Act PDF returned a 403 error and could not be fetched to check for an explicit statutory age provision. No authoritative source was found conclusively confirming either interpretation. Original score of 1 (>17) is retained as unconfirmed pending access to the primary legal text; flagged for human review given the conflicting signals between design intent (birth-to-death) and the currently observed adult-focused rollout.
revised_comments: The minimum enrollment age for Somalia's national digital ID is not explicitly stated in publicly available NIRA materials. Current rollout and mandated use cases - including passport applications (from September 2025) and domestic travel (from January 2026) - are oriented towards the adult population, while the underlying digital ID policy documentation envisages the system eventually providing identity 'from birth to death' with links to civil registration.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: The NIRA Act (Law 009/2023) states that eligibility extends to 'citizens of the Federal Republic of Somalia and anyone who is a legal resident of the country, except for those who are on a short visit.' The ID policy document (2019 TOR) also states 'All residents of Somalia will be eligible for enrollment, irrespective of citizenship status.' Legal residents and refugees with legal status are eligible, but not all non-nationals (e.g., short-term visitors are excluded). This represents 'some' non-nationals being eligible.
revision_notes: The mof.gov.so Digital ID Legal Framework TOR (fetched) confirms the intended eligibility design: 'All residents of Somalia will be eligible for enrollment, irrespective of citizenship status', with eligibility criteria to specify inclusion regardless of citizenship. NIRA's registration page (fetched) describes diaspora and resident-oriented registration; NIRA's main site (fetched) refers to providing identity to 'every citizen and legal resident', implying short-term visitors or those without legal residency are excluded. The NIRA Act PDF returned a 403 error and could not be independently fetched to confirm the precise statutory wording on non-national categories (e.g. refugees, asylum seekers). Available evidence supports 'Some' (legal residents included, short-term visitors excluded) rather than 'All' or 'None'. Score of 2 (Some) confirmed.
revised_comments: Non-nationals with legal residency status, not only citizens, are eligible to register for Somalia's national digital ID. Design documentation for the ID system states that all residents are eligible for enrolment irrespective of citizenship status, while NIRA's operational materials describe the system as serving 'every citizen and legal resident'. Short-term visitors and those without legal residency status are not covered.
